config.plugin.name: pgoutput
config.publication.name: streaming_cdc
config.slot.name: streaming_cdc_slot
config.heartbeat.action.query: INSERT INTO streaming.debezium_heartbeat (ts) VALUES (now()) ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET ts = now()
config.errors.deadletterqueue.topic.name: dlq.cdc.postgres

_notes.heartbeat.interval.ms: Without heartbeats, a replication slot on a low-traffic table holds the WAL open and the RDS volume fills up. This is the single most common way a CDC pipeline takes down its own source database.
_notes.publication.autocreate.mode: Disabled on purpose. The publication is owned by migrations (003_publication.sql), not by the connector, so a connector restart can never silently widen what we replicate.
_notes.snapshot.locking.mode: none is safe here because pgoutput snapshots run in a repeatable-read transaction; it avoids taking an ACCESS SHARE lock storm on a live OLTP database.
_notes.delete.handling.mode: rewrite keeps a __deleted flag on the record instead of dropping it, so the warehouse can model soft deletes rather than losing rows silently.
